Muscles store only enough glycogen for about ninety minutes of hard running, so a marathon needs carbohydrate on the way. Aim for sixty to ninety grams per hour from gels or sports drink, starting early rather than waiting for fatigue. Practise the exact products during long runs so the stomach is used to them. Carb loading in the two days before the race tops up glycogen. Drink to thirst and take some sodium in hot weather. This is the part of the [[Marathon training plan]] people most often skip.
